rows.title: Ballads and Songs
rows.evidence: djvu title page: 'BALLADS AND SONGS 1894 LONDON. JOHN LANE THE BODLEY HEAD BOSTON: COPELAND & DAY'; contents list Thirty Bob a Week, A Ballad of a Nun; collection cdl/americana
rows.case: Bloom lists Davidson's Ballads and Songs; not on PG. The 1894 Lane/Copeland & Day first edition is on IA with an OCR layer.
rows.note: Alternates: balladssongs00daviuoft (dated 1898 in IA metadata, unread). Only Fleet Street Eclogues is held (mason-poetry).

rows.title: The Poems and Prose of Ernest Dowson, With a Memoir by Arthur Symons
rows.evidence: PG header read: no copyright notice; contains all verse collections (Verses, Decorations, The Pierrot of the Minute) plus prose
rows.case: Bloom lists Dowson's Complete Poems; PG 8497 is the standard Symons collected Poems and Prose.
rows.note: Our 'dowson' shelf holds only his translations. PG header gives no source imprint year; Symons memoir dates from 1905 Lane edition (not read).

rows.title: The Plays of Ivan S. Turgenev, translated from the Russian by M. S. Mandell
rows.evidence: djvu title page read; 'A MONTH IN THE COUNTRY' appears at line 16481 of the djvu text; collection internetarchivebooks
rows.case: Mandell's 1924 Plays of Turgenev was the first English version of the plays and has A Month in the Country complete.
rows.note: Macmillan NY issue (IA playsofivansturg0001msma, 'Copyright 1924') is only vol. I of the two-volume printing. Garnett's 1934 Three Plays version isn't PD. A Garnett text at IA 'AMonthInTheCountry' has no imprint, so rejected.

rows.title: Poetical Works of William Cullen Bryant, Household Edition
rows.year: 1880 (title page in PG text; copyright entries 1854, 1871)
rows.evidence: PG title page read
rows.case: Bryant's collected Household Edition, revised in his lifetime, is on PG and isn't held.
rows.note: Alternative: PG 16341 'Poems by William Cullen Bryant' (imprint unread).

rows.title: The Works of John Greenleaf Whittier, Complete
rows.evidence: PG text opens with the Standard Library Edition publishers' advertisement (Riverside, revised by Whittier); vols I-IV are the poems (also PG 9567, 9574, 9580, 9586 one volume each)
rows.case: The Riverside/Standard Library Edition is Whittier's own final arrangement of his poems; not held.
rows.note: If only the verse is wanted, take PG 9567, 9574, 9580 and 9586 (vols I-IV) instead of the complete 9600.

rows.title: Nature
rows.year: 1849 (copyright entry on PG title page: 'Entered ... in the year 1849'; 'New Edition', Boston & Cambridge)
rows.evidence: PG title page read
rows.case: Nature is on PG; the rwemerson shelf holds only the two Essays series.
rows.note: 1849 'new edition' (Nature, Addresses, and Lectures) includes Nature itself.

rows.title: Representative Men: Seven Lectures
rows.evidence: PG header read; no imprint in front matter
rows.case: Representative Men is on PG; not held.

rows.title: The Conduct of Life
rows.year: 1871 (PG title page: Boston 1871; 'Entered ... in the year 1860')
rows.evidence: PG title page read
rows.case: The Conduct of Life is on PG; not held.
rows.note: The machine's held hit (Wisdom of the East, Confucius) is a false match.

rows.title: Journals of Ralph Waldo Emerson, with annotations, ed. Edward Waldo Emerson and Waldo Emerson Forbes, vol. I, 1820-1824
rows.year: 1909 (title page: Boston and New York, Houghton Mifflin, 1909; 'Copyright, 1909')
rows.evidence: djvu title page read; collection toronto
rows.case: The ten-volume Emerson/Forbes Journals (1909-14) was the standard edition until the Harvard JMN. All volumes are pre-1931 and on IA.
rows.note: Ten volumes. Only vol. I's title page was read; the other nine need picking from IA (e.g. the cu31924021990* Cornell series, 1909-14 per IA metadata).

rows.title: Poems, Household Edition
rows.evidence: PG front matter lists copyright years 1867, 1876, 1883, 1895, 1904 and 1911, so this is the 1904/1911 Centenary-text Household Edition
rows.case: Emerson's poems collected (Centenary text, with appendix); not held.
rows.note: Also PG 15963 May-Day, and Other Pieces (1867).

rows.title: The Complete Poems of Emily Dickinson, with an introduction by her niece Martha Dickinson Bianchi
rows.evidence: djvu title page and copyright page read; collection internetarchivebooks
rows.case: Bianchi's 1924 Complete Poems was the fullest pre-1931 edition. The PG Three Series is the clean-text fallback.
rows.note: Both are edited (regularised) texts, not the Johnson 1955 manuscript text (not PD). Nothing by Dickinson is held. Another 1924 scan: completepoemsofe00dick_1 (LoC), which has a garbled OCR front.

rows.title: Poems by Emily Dickinson, Three Series, Complete
rows.evidence: PG header read; the 1890-96 Todd/Higginson selection
rows.case: Bianchi's 1924 Complete Poems was the fullest pre-1931 edition. The PG Three Series is the clean-text fallback.
rows.note: Both are edited (regularised) texts, not the Johnson 1955 manuscript text (not PD). Nothing by Dickinson is held. Another 1924 scan: completepoemsofe00dick_1 (LoC), which has a garbled OCR front.

rows.title: Complete Prose Works: Specimen Days and Collect, November Boughs and Goodbye My Fancy
rows.evidence: PG header read
rows.case: Specimen Days leads off Whitman's Complete Prose Works on PG; not held.

rows.title: Clarel: a poem and pilgrimage in the Holy Land, vol. I (Works of Herman Melville, Standard Edition, vol. XIV)
rows.evidence: djvu title page read; notes 'CLAREL was first published in 1876 (New York: G. P. Putnam's Sons)'; collection internetarchivebooks
rows.case: Clarel isn't on PG. The 1924 Constable Standard Edition reprints the 1876 text in two volumes on IA.
rows.note: No scan of the 1876 Putnam first was found.

rows.title: The Complete Works of Edgar Allan Poe, ed. James A. Harrison (Virginia Edition), vol. VIII: Literary Criticism, vol. I
rows.year: 1902 (title page: New York, Thomas Y. Crowell; 'Copyright, 1902')
rows.evidence: djvu title page and contents read (reviews of Bryant, Horse-Shoe Robinson, I Promessi Sposi...); collection BYU/americana
rows.case: The Virginia Edition's five Literary Criticism volumes (VIII-XII) plus Marginalia (XVI) are the fullest pre-1931 Poe criticism. The held Raven Edition carries only a few essays.
rows.note: Vols IX-XII still to pick; IA has completeworksed00harrgoog (vol. IX) and completeworksed05poegoog (vol. XII) per IA metadata, unread. The machine's held hit (Hodge, Princeton Review) is a false match.

rows.title: Virginia Edition vol. XVI: Marginalia; Eureka

rows.title: Essays and Poems, by Jones Very
rows.year: 1839 (title page: Boston, Charles C. Little and James Brown, MDCCCXXXIX)
rows.evidence: djvu title page and contents read (Epic Poetry, Shakspeare, Hamlet; poems); collection cdl/americana
rows.case: This is Bloom's exact title, the 1839 first edition edited by Emerson; not on PG.
rows.note: The fuller 1886 Poems and Essays (Clarke) exists (IA poemsessays00very), but that scan's front OCR is garbled.

rows.title: Poems, by Frederick Goddard Tuckerman
rows.year: 1864 (title page: Boston, Ticknor and Fields, 1864; note 'first collected and printed in 1860')
rows.evidence: djvu title page and contents read; collection library_of_congress/americana
rows.case: Tuckerman's only lifetime book, the Poems (1860/1864), holds the sonnet sequences that make up most of Bloom's 'other poems'.
rows.note: 'The Cricket' itself was first printed in 1950 (from knowledge), so it isn't PD and isn't in this volume. Flag that the title is only partly covered.

rows.title: Poems of Nature, ed. Henry S. Salt and Frank B. Sanborn
rows.evidence: PG title page shows Boston and New York / London: John Lane; year not on the lines read
rows.case: Salt and Sanborn's Poems of Nature (1895, from knowledge) was the first collection of Thoreau's verse; not held.
rows.note: Alternative: PG 42553 Excursions, and Poems (Writings vol. 5, 1906).

rows.case: Thoreau's two posthumous essay collections; only Walden and Civil Disobedience are held.
rows.note: The machine's PG candidate (Oxford Book of American Essays) is an anthology; not used.

rows.title: Each in His Own Way and Two Other Plays
rows.year: 1923 (title page: New York, E. P. Dutton; 'Copyright, 1923')
rows.evidence: djvu title page read; collection trent_university/internetarchivebooks
rows.case: Four of Naked Masks' five plays came out in English in 1922-23: Six Characters, Henry IV, It Is So (Right You Are) and Each in His Own Way.
rows.note: Liolà, the fifth, was first Englished in Bentley's 1952 Naked Masks (from knowledge), so it isn't PD. Already held: livingston: One-Act Plays and The Late Mattia Pascal.

rows.title: Confessions of Zeno
rows.year: 1930 (PG front matter: 'Copyright 1930 by Alfred A. Knopf, Inc.'; PG header 'Original publication: New York: New Directions/Alfred A. Knopf, 1930')
rows.evidence: PG header and copyright line read
rows.case: De Zoete's 1930 Knopf translation predates the 1931 line; PG has it.
rows.note: PG lists Renato Poggioli as commentator, so the source copy may be a later New Directions printing with Poggioli's note (that note is post-1931). Ship the translation and drop or check the Poggioli matter.

rows.title: The Life of Don Quixote and Sancho according to Miguel de Cervantes Saavedra, expounded with comment by Miguel de Unamuno
rows.year: 1927 (title page: New York & London, Alfred A. Knopf, 1927; 'Copyright 1927')
rows.evidence: djvu title page and contents read; collection marygrovecollege/internetarchivebooks/americana
rows.case: Bloom's 'Our Lord Don Quixote' is the Bollingen volume built round Vida de Don Quijote y Sancho. Earle's 1927 Knopf translation of that book is PD and on IA.
rows.note: The Bollingen volume adds essays not in Earle; those aren't covered. Second copy: lifeofdonquixote0000migu_o2k7.

rows.title: Penguin Island
rows.evidence: PG header read; it names no translator
rows.case: Penguin Island (1908) is on PG; not held.
rows.note: PG header gives no translator. The English Penguin Island of 1909 (Lane) is by A. W. Evans (from knowledge, not read). Confirm before shelving.

rows.title: The Wanderer
rows.evidence: PG header and title page read; intro by Havelock Ellis
rows.case: Delisle's 1928 The Wanderer is the first English Grand Meaulnes and is on PG.
rows.note: Havelock Ellis's introduction is part of the 1928 edition, so it's PD too.

rows.bloom_title: Remembrance of Things Past (In Search of Lost Time)
rows.title: Cities of the Plain (Modern Library)
rows.year: unread (copyright line 'COPYRIGHT, 1927, BY RANDOM HOUSE'; Modern Library printing, date unread)
rows.evidence: djvu front matter read; one-volume complete text
rows.case: Four of Scott Moncrieff's volumes are held. Cities of the Plain (1927) and The Sweet Cheat Gone (1930) are also PD and complete the run through vol. 6.
rows.note: Time Regained (Stephen Hudson, 1931) is NOT PD, so the run can only stop at The Sweet Cheat Gone. Scans are of later printings that copyright the text 1927/1930 and look unrevised; no 1930 first-edition scan was found for Sweet Cheat Gone (sweetcheatgone0000marc is a 1970 Vintage). Rule 6 call: these are Modern Library reprints.
